svg.text: Flywheel next — three security designs: what we keep warm between ticks, under which key, and who can read what

the customer is protecting against our staff, a co-tenant, a compromised shared component and the cloud provider · the shared tier is fast because it does not re-clone every tick, and that warm copy is the thing a customer is right to ask about · the three designs differ in one thing — where the key lives and who may unwrap it
options (a) and (f) · a key per organization over every store the shared tier touches · the recommended default · tiers 1 and 2
the same binary whenever you run it · sign-in is GitHub device flow
raw capture material and the triage session that reads it stay here (263)
state and blueprints, created under the customer's own account (219)
held under GitHub's own key, as every repository on the platform is
the batch ticker over a warm cache · sparse minimised clone: manifest,
register, leases, the sink's mark, flywheel/ — a read outside it is a refusal (262)
one organization each (241) · the only place code is ever cloned (264)
triage runs here or on the laptop (263) · retire destroys the host and its disk (240)
not used · the customer places no secret at all, and chat runs through the platform's bot
WHAT WE KEEP WARM, AND UNDER WHICH KEY
one KMS key per organization, held by the service · its policy names only the role that ticks that organization
clone cache · state in full, blueprints blobless and sparse · 10–50 MB
that key · the queue holds an id and a pointer
times and ids, no content by construction (245)
that key · host and disk destroyed at retire (240)
unwrapped only for the duration of a tick, by a role scoped to that one organization (257, 259)
idle past a stated time the cache is evicted, so a sleeping tenant has nothing warm to steal; its next tick re-clones (258)
the residual, stated plainly: that organization's plaintext for that tick, and any other ticking in the same process at that moment
a GitHub repository reader reads records unless the organization declares (c) — a GitHub question, not a shared-tier one
WHAT WE CAN TELL THE CUSTOMER
“Everything we hold about you is encrypted at rest under a key that exists for your
organization alone, and it is unwrapped only while your plan is being evaluated — a
stolen disk or a leaked snapshot of ours is ciphertext.”
design A with the key moved into the customer's account under a revocable grant (b), plus (d) where wanted · tiers 2 and 3
the same binary · unchanged from A, and unchanged by the upgrade
raw capture material and triage stay off every shared host (263)
their two repositories, under GitHub's own key — unchanged from A
option (c) is available here as a declaration, for a customer whose concern is GitHub
the same warm cache, sealed the same way · the ticker holds a revocable grant,
not a key · optionally a Nitro enclave releasing the key only to the attested image (d)
one organization each (241) · code here only, destroyed at retire (240, 264)
the KMS key, and the raw capture store as a bucket they own
every use of it logged in their account · RevokeGrant ends our access in minutes
WHAT WE KEEP WARM, AND UNDER WHICH KEY
the customer's own KMS key, reached by a grant under an encryption context naming the organization
clone cache · the same 10–50 MB, kept the same way
their key · id and pointer only
a revoked or unreachable key fails closed: no tick proceeds on state it cannot open, one attention line names it
and since when, work already running is not interrupted, and nothing is ever kept unencrypted as a fallback (260)
both amber cells go dark with (d): the enclave releases the key only to an attested image, which removes our staff and a compromised
image from the set entirely · without it, staff read while the grant stands and never once it is revoked
WHAT WE CAN TELL THE CUSTOMER
“Everything above, plus the key is yours — we cannot use it once you revoke it, and
revocation stops us reading anything, anywhere, within minutes, with no ticket and
no waiting on a deletion job.”
option (e) · we provision the binary into their account, hold no content, and keep nothing warm at all · tier 3
the same binary, the same manifest, the same repositories they already have
moving here is not a migration — the data keys are re-wrapped and history is left alone
their App, their installation, their two repositories
under GitHub's own key here too · ciphertext only if they also declare (c)
a control plane only — it keeps nothing warm, because it holds no content
the organization's name, its health and its billing counters, and nothing else
theirs, in their account, at whatever bound they set · no co-tenant exists to isolate from
the whole thing: ticker, cache, pools, key, raw store and bot — provisioned through
a role they grant with an external id, and revocable by withdrawing that role
WHAT WE KEEP WARM, AND UNDER WHICH KEY
their key, in their account, never shared with us — we hold no key, no grant and no copy
raw capture store · pool host disks
what stays ours is the supply chain: our binary still runs there
and the price is blind support — we cannot see what broke, and we will say so rather than ask for a copy
the provider is now their provider and their problem · no co-tenant exists and no shared ticker exists to compromise
what we keep is the bill, not the content
WHAT WE CAN TELL THE CUSTOMER
“If you would rather we held nothing at all, we provision the whole thing into your
account and keep only your organization's name, its health and its bill.”
conditional — for one organization and one tick, or while a grant stands
no such party exists in this design
where the key lives — the one thing the three designs differ in

recommended default for the hosted tier is Design A: a key per organization over every warm store, unwrapped only while that organization's plan is being evaluated, plus minimisation and pool and triage isolation · it answers what a customer actually asks — what sits on your disks between ticks and who can read it — without asking them to do anything

Design B is a key-provider swap on top of it, not a re-architecture · envelopes in git (option c) are a declaration a customer turns on when their concern is GitHub rather than us, and never the default (265, 266) · none of this is a migration: every tier seals the same stores the same way and what changes is where the key lives · 256 – 266 · §2 and §4 of proposals/security.md
